I am 75 this year, and I have worked my 5.2 mu of land in Quzhou for 55 years. My wife and me, we are the only ones left in the house now — our children went to the city. I finished middle school, so I can read the numbers on the fertilizer bags and understand what the seed dealer tells me, but I still farm the way my father taught me. I watch what my neighbors do, and they watch me. That is how I know what works.

I grow winter wheat and summer maize on the same land. That is the only rotation that makes sense here. Wheat goes in after October 1st, and maize goes in right after wheat harvest in early June. I cannot leave the ground empty — I need two crops to pay for our living.

For wheat this year, I will buy improved seed from the county supply cooperative — Jimai or Liangxing, whatever they have that my neighbor Lao Zhang says did well last year. I will hire the rotary tiller after the maize stalks are chopped and spread. For base fertilizer, I will put down one 50-kilogram bag of compound fertilizer for every two mu — so for my 5.2 mu I need three bags total, which is about 100 jin per mu. The bag says 16-16-16, so that gives nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium all together. Then when the wheat greens up in March and starts jointing, I will topdress with urea — one 40-kilogram bag of urea for every two mu, which is 40 jin per mu. I know some people say that is a bit much, but three years ago when I tried to save money and used less, the wheat turned yellow and thin, and I lost almost 100 jin per mu. I will not make that mistake again. A few extra yuan on fertilizer is nothing compared to a bad harvest.

For water, I pump from my well. Electricity costs real money, so I do not waste water, but wheat cannot dry out in spring. I will irrigate three times: once at green-up in late March, once at jointing in April, and once at heading in early May. Three times is what I have always done, and it is enough if I flood it properly. For pesticides, I spray herbicide once in early spring when the wheat is still small, and I spray once more in April for aphids or rust if I see yellow spots — that is two sprays.

For maize, I buy hybrid seed bags — Zhengdan 958 or Xianyu 335, whatever the shop has with the blue label that germinated well last year. After wheat harvest in June, I direct-seed into the stubble without plowing. No-tillage saves diesel and time, and at my age I cannot rush around behind a plow in the summer heat. For fertilizer, I put 80 jin of compound per mu at planting — that is one 40-kilogram bag for every mu, roughly. Then when the maize is knee-high at the big-flare stage, I side-dress urea — about 30 jin per mu. Again, I would rather put a little too much than too little. The summer rains usually come, so I only irrigate twice: once if June is dry right after planting, and once at tasseling in July. For maize, I spray herbicide right after emergence, and I spray once for corn borer in mid-July. Two sprays total.

I expect my wheat to yield about 1,000 jin per mu — that is 500 kilograms per mu — and my maize to yield about 1,100 jin per mu, or 550 kilograms per mu. Last year was about the same. I am too old to gamble on new methods. I will do what I know, spend what I need to spend, and hope the weather holds.
